claim: The most commonly reported factors associated with FT were: being female, younger age, low income at baseline, adjuvant therapies and more recent diagnosis.

evidence.quote: Younger age (4.23, 95%CI 2.20 to 6.26, p < 0.001), lower earnings at diagnosis (1.17, 95%CI 0.76 to 1.58, p < 0.001), and loss in earnings (-1.80, 95%CI -2.43 to -1.16, p < 0.001) were associated with worse FT.
evidence.note: Supports younger age and lower income only; head and neck survivors; no sex, adjuvant therapy or recency.

claim: The rates of anxiety and depression were higher among caregivers of cancer patients than they were for caregivers of other types of patients.

evidence.quote: Caregivers of cancer patients are at greater risk of developing depression than the general population.
evidence.note: Higher depression risk vs general population, not vs caregivers of other conditions; anxiety not compared.

evidence.quote: In the current review, the pooled prevalence of depression among caregivers of Cancer patients was 42.08% (95% CI: 34.71-49.45).
evidence.note: Gives depression prevalence in cancer caregivers; no comparison with other caregivers, no anxiety.

claim: Existing interventions are effective in achieving modest increases in physical activity at least 3 months post-intervention completion.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, preferring exercising with others at M0 was associated with greater increases in self-reported MVPA between M0 and M6 (124.2 ± 152 vs. 53.1 ± 113.8, p = 0.014).
evidence.note: Reports MVPA increases at 3-month follow-up (M6) after a breast cancer survivor intervention, but as a preference subgroup comparison.

evidence.quote: At 3-month follow-up, all patient-reported outcomes and physical fitness variables remained significantly improved compared to baseline in the exercise group (p < 0.01).
evidence.note: Fitness and patient-reported outcomes stayed improved at 3 months; physical activity level itself not reported.

claim: In one study, 163 women with metastatic breast cancer reported a total of 530 physical impairments that were not detected during hospitalization, but which required physical therapy and/or occupational therapy.

evidence.quote: Ninety-two percent of patients (150 of 163) had at least one physical impairment. Among 530 identified impairments, 484 (92%) required a physical rehabilitation intervention and 469 (88%) required physical therapy (PT) and/or occupational therapy (OT).
evidence.note: Matches 163 women and 530 impairments, but 530 is all identified impairments; not stated as undetected during hospitalization.

claim: A cancer transition is clearly underway in countries transiting to high levels of income and development whereby reductions in infection-related cancers are offset by concomitant increases in cancers linked to a "Westernization" of lifestyle.

evidence.quote: The incidence of westernized lifestyle-related cancers in China (i.e. colorectal cancer, prostate, bladder cancer) has risen but the incidence of the digestive cancers has decreased from 2000 to 2011.
evidence.note: one instance: China shows rising westernized-lifestyle cancers and falling digestive cancers; "offset" not stated and only one country.

claim: Prevention Potential : More than 90% of cancers are directly attributable to environmental and lifestyle factors, making them largely preventable.

evidence.quote: Yet, the majority of CRC is sporadic and largely attributable to the constellation of modifiable environmental risk factors characterizing westernization (for example, obesity, physical inactivity, poor diets, alcohol drinking and smoking).
evidence.note: Majority attributable to modifiable environmental factors, but for colorectal cancer only, no 90% figure.

evidence.quote: These results suggest that only a third of the variation in cancer risk among tissues is attributable to environmental factors or inherited predispositions.
evidence.note: Concerns variation in risk among tissues, not share of cancers; no 90% figure.
